\chapter{When You Are Lost}
\label{ch:ta-when-you-are-lost}
\hlchaptermodality{94}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say I do not understand, ask someone to write it down, ask for one more time, and ask what they said.}

\section[puriyavillai]{\ta{புரியவில்லை} (puriyavillai) — I don't understand}

\label{lesson:TA-C94-dontunderstand}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for please show me, then the Tamil for I did not hear it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{புரியவில்லை}}
\textbf{\ta{புரியவில்லை}} (\emph{puriyavillai}) — \textquotedblleft{}I don't understand\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}it did not become clear\textquotedblright{}.

The most useful sentence a learner owns. It also ends in \textbf{\ta{இல்லை}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The honest sentence every learner needs.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puriyavillai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puriyavillai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{puriyavillai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for please show me, then the Tamil for I did not hear it, then say \emph{puriyavillai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{புரியவில்லை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}I don't understand\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[eḻutuṅkaḷ]{\ta{எழுதுங்கள்} (eḻutuṅkaḷ) — please write it}

\label{lesson:TA-C94-write}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for I did not hear it, then the Tamil for I don't understand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{எழுதுங்கள்}}
\textbf{\ta{எழுதுங்கள்}} (\emph{eḻutuṅkaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}please write (it)\textquotedblright{}.

It shares its root with \textbf{\ta{எழுத்து}}, \textquotedblleft{}a letter of the script\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ta{இங்கே} \ta{எழுதுங்கள்}} — \textquotedblleft{}please write it here\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A request to see the word.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eḻutuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eḻutuṅkaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{iṅkē eḻutuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for I did not hear it, then the Tamil for I don't understand, then say \emph{eḻutuṅkaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{எழுதுங்கள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please write it\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[iṉṉoru muṟai]{\ta{இன்னொரு} \ta{முறை} (iṉṉoru muṟai) — one more time}

\label{lesson:TA-C94-onemoretime}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for I don't understand, then the Tamil for please write it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இன்னொரு} \ta{முறை}}
\textbf{\ta{இன்னொரு} \ta{முறை}} (\emph{iṉṉoru muṟai}) — \textquotedblleft{}one more time\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{இன்னொரு}} is \textquotedblleft{}another\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ta{முறை}} is \textquotedblleft{}a time, a turn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Once more, politely.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṉṉoru muṟai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṉṉoru muṟai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{iṉṉoru muṟai colluṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for I don't understand, then the Tamil for please write it, then say \emph{iṉṉoru muṟai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{இன்னொரு} \ta{முறை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}One more time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[eṉṉa coṉṉīrkaḷ?]{\ta{என்ன} \ta{சொன்னீர்கள்}? (eṉṉa coṉṉīrkaḷ?) — what did you say?}

\label{lesson:TA-C94-whatsaid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for please write it, then the Tamil for one more time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{என்ன} \ta{சொன்னீர்கள்}?}
\textbf{\ta{என்ன} \ta{சொன்னீர்கள்}?} (\emph{eṉṉa coṉṉīrkaḷ?}) — \textquotedblleft{}what did you say?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{என்ன}} is \textquotedblleft{}what\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ta{சொன்னீர்கள்}} is \textquotedblleft{}you said\textquotedblright{}, respectfully.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Don't understand, write it, one more time, what did you say.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṉṉa coṉṉīrkaḷ?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṉṉa coṉṉīrkaḷ?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{eṉṉa coṉṉīrkaḷ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for please write it, then the Tamil for one more time, then say \emph{eṉṉa coṉṉīrkaḷ?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{என்ன} \ta{சொன்னீர்கள்}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}What did you say?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
